observations: unregister sets LED_UNREGISTERING and calls led_set_brightness(LED_OFF) unless LED_RETAIN_AT_SHUTDOWN is set
unregister flushes led_cdev->set_brightness_work, then unregisters the LED device
when brightness_set is present, __led_set_brightness invokes it synchronously
the driver callback can enqueue a separate driver work item before the LED class device is unregistered
the bus or driver remove callback runs in device_remove
device_unbind_cleanup calls devres_release_all after device_remove returns
the stock probe passes allocation flags 0xdc0 to devm_kmalloc; this includes the __GFP_ZERO bit
the embedded LED classdev flags start at zero unless the driver sets them

locations: 0x572c-0x5744 initialization of work at state+0x428 and its callback
callback locks state and accesses chip operations and fields
0x87c4 sets state+0x6 to 1 on successful RAM firmware update
no LED unregister or second state+0x428 cancellation follows that point

candidate_evidence.observation: semantic source mirror matches the stock callback offsets and queue_work_on arguments
candidate remove cancels state+0x428 before misc deregistration and has no LED devres teardown step

execution_order: Probe allocates the 0x6f8-byte state with zeroing flags; vibrator_init embeds led_classdev at state+0xa8 and registers it as a managed LED on the I2C device.
A successful ram_load sets state+0x6 to 1. The stock brightness_set callback uses that bit as its admission condition and queues state+0x428 on state+0x448.
aw_remove synchronously cancels state+0x428 and returns without unregistering the managed LED.
The target driver core invokes devres_release_all after remove returns. The LED devres release calls led_classdev_unregister.
Unless LED_RETAIN_AT_SHUTDOWN is set, LED unregister calls led_set_brightness(LED_OFF). The target LED core directly invokes brightness_set when present.
With state+0x6 still set, brightness_set can queue state+0x428 after aw_remove has already canceled it. The LED core flushes only its own set_brightness_work; it does not drain this driver work item.

finding.title: managed LED unregister can resubmit vibrator work after remove cancellation
finding.condition: successful RAM initialization leaves state+0x6 bit 0 set at unbind, and the LED is not marked LED_RETAIN_AT_SHUTDOWN; the reviewed driver init does not set that retain flag
finding.impact: the vibrator worker can run after remove has returned, access state and chip operations during teardown, or race the devres release of the state allocation

limits: This is a statically confirmed callback and workqueue path with a readiness-state condition; scheduler-dependent runtime manifestation has not been reproduced.
The conclusion is bound to the pinned target kernel source and the stock module evidence listed above.
The existing per-device workqueue release review separately records that aw_remove does not destroy the queue at state+0x448.
No reconstruction source changed and no Docker rebuild was run for this read-only review.
hardening_follow_up: Keep the stock-exact candidate unchanged and implement fixes in a separately identified hardening candidate.
Set a per-device dying gate before teardown and make brightness_set refuse new queue submissions once teardown starts.
Unregister the LED interface while state remains valid, then stop asynchronous producers and synchronously drain state+0x428 after the LED callback can no longer enqueue it.
Drain or otherwise lifetime-pin firmware callbacks before releasing state, then destroy the per-device workqueue before devres frees its owning state.
